inclusion_checks.evidence: The report presents Orion, a collaborative inference framework with system formulation, algorithms, and evaluation.
The architecture uses a heterogeneous UAV swarm with multiple UAV onboard devices and a ground/cloud comparison node.
LLM inference is distributed through layer partitioning, sequence partitioning, and predictive decoding across edge devices.
The study provides a Python simulation and reported latency evaluation with named baselines.
Publisher header gives 26 May 2026, within 2021-01-01 through 2026-11-25.
The publisher HTML is in English.
The article is presented as a journal article in Drones 2026, 10(6), 410.

exclusion_checks.evidence: The body evaluates inference execution; it is not a training-only or federated-learning study.
Model layer partitioning and distributed LLM inference are explicit, so this is not indivisible generic offloading.
The evaluated architecture is multi-device and multi-UAV rather than single-UAV-only perception.
The workload is LLM inference and the body evaluates compute/network behavior, not communication-only routing or caching.
The report is a journal article with full publisher HTML body, not an editorial, tutorial, abstract-only record, thesis, patent, book chapter, or review.

extraction.architecture_and_uav_role: Heterogeneous UAV swarm and edge-only collaborative inference; Section 4.1 models three NVIDIA AGX Orin modules and one Orin NX module as the UAV swarm, with a cloud base station used for comparison. Locator: Section 4.1, lines 561-567, https://www.mdpi.com/2504-446X/10/6/410
extraction.exact_inference_topology: Pipeline-parallel distributed LLM inference across selected edge devices; contiguous layer blocks are assigned to distinct devices, with activation transfer between stages. Locator: Section 3.1, lines 262-292, https://www.mdpi.com/2504-446X/10/6/410
extraction.model_and_dataset: Llama-2 7B, 13B, and 70B; simulated UAV sensor traces and variable sensor-log lengths. No named public dataset reported. Locator: Section 4.1, lines 568-568, and Section 4.2, lines 596-606, https://www.mdpi.com/2504-446X/10/6/410
extraction.partition_granularity: Contiguous model-layer blocks plus non-uniform input-sequence chunks; predictive decoding operates at token level. Locator: Sections 3.1-3.3, lines 262-323 and 407-560, https://www.mdpi.com/2504-446X/10/6/410
extraction.decision_variables_objective_constraints: Choose edge-device subset, contiguous layer intervals, and sequence chunk boundaries; minimize maximum pipeline-stage computation-plus-communication latency subject to per-device memory capacity. Locator: Section 3.1, lines 277-292; Section 3.2, lines 421-444, https://www.mdpi.com/2504-446X/10/6/410
extraction.solver: State-compressed dynamic programming for device/layer partitioning and min-max dynamic programming for sequence partitioning; predictive decoding uses speculative execution. Locator: Sections 3.1-3.3, lines 293-323, 427-449, and 491-560, https://www.mdpi.com/2504-446X/10/6/410
extraction.mobility_channel_failure_assumptions: Inter-UAV bandwidth is varied from 400-1000 Mb/s with ±20% fluctuation; air-to-ground bandwidth is varied from 100-400 Mb/s. Section 4.8 models computation and communication noise, but no UAV-failure recovery experiment is reported. Predictive-decoding rollback concerns incorrect token speculation, not UAV failure recovery. Locator: https://www.mdpi.com/2504-446X/10/6/410, Sections 4.1, 4.4-4.5, 4.7-4.8, lines 565-567, 617-635, 647-659.
extraction.evaluation_setup: Python 3.13.5 simulation of five heterogeneous devices, Llama-2 7B/13B/70B, sensor-log lengths, bandwidth settings, prediction-accuracy break-even/rollback evaluation, and environmental-noise sensitivity evaluation. No measured onboard execution or physical flight validation. Locator: https://www.mdpi.com/2504-446X/10/6/410, Sections 4.1-4.8, lines 561-659; Section 5.5, lines 689-693.
extraction.baselines: Edge-Solo, Cloud-Edge-Even, Cloud-Edge-Opt, EdgeShard, and Jupiter. Locator: Section 4.1, lines 570-590, https://www.mdpi.com/2504-446X/10/6/410
extraction.metric_definitions: Primary outcome is prefill/end-to-end latency; Section 4.7 evaluates prediction-accuracy break-even using rollback overhead, while Section 4.8 compares static-partition latency with re-optimized latency under computation and communication noise. Locator: https://www.mdpi.com/2504-446X/10/6/410, Sections 3.1 and 3.3, lines 267-292 and 551-560; Sections 4.7-4.8, lines 647-659.
extraction.units: Latency is reported in milliseconds; bandwidth is reported in Mb/s; sensor input length is reported in tokens; memory is reported in GB; compute capability is reported in TFLOPS. Locator: Sections 3.1 and 4.1-4.2, lines 267-292 and 565-606, https://www.mdpi.com/2504-446X/10/6/410
extraction.repeated_runs_seeds: Section 4.7 reports 300 Monte Carlo simulations per configuration; Section 4.8 reports N=100 independent trials for each nominal-noise and extreme-noise scenario. Random seeds are not located. Locator: https://www.mdpi.com/2504-446X/10/6/410, Sections 4.7-4.8, lines 647-659.
extraction.outcome_conditions: Section 4.7 uses Llama-2 13B, 64-token input, 1000 Mb/s inter-UAV bandwidth with ±20% fluctuation, and 300 simulations per configuration. evaluation_coverage.note: Python 3.13.5 simulation; five heterogeneous devices; inter-UAV bandwidth 400-1000 Mb/s with ±20% fluctuation; air-to-ground bandwidth 100-400 Mb/s; Llama-2 scales and sensor-log lengths are specified.
Evaluates latency across Llama-2 7B, 13B, and 70B with 64-token input, 1000 Mb/s inter-UAV bandwidth, and 200 Mb/s air-to-ground bandwidth.
Evaluates Llama-2 13B latency for 16, 32, 64, and 128 tokens with 1000 Mb/s inter-UAV bandwidth and ±20% fluctuation.
Evaluates Llama-2 13B latency under 100, 150, 200, and 400 Mb/s air-to-ground bandwidth with fixed inter-UAV bandwidth.
Evaluates Llama-2 13B latency under 400, 600, 800, and 1000 Mb/s inter-UAV bandwidth with 200 Mb/s air-to-ground bandwidth.
Ablation compares full Orion, Orion without adaptive sequence partitioning, and Orion without predictive decoding across 7B, 13B, and 70B models.
Prediction-accuracy break-even/rollback evaluation uses 300 Monte Carlo simulations per configuration; rollback refers to incorrect speculative-token prediction, not UAV-failure recovery.
Environmental-noise sensitivity uses computation and communication perturbations, nominal and extreme noise settings, and 100 independent trials per scenario.
